exact_quote: Within that, nothing is off the table. Any language, any framework. Pre-trained models, commercial or open. LLMs, hosted or local. External data about other games. Your own detection, tracking or event-recognition models.
implication: External models and external games are allowed when organizers can inspect and the technical document explains them.

exact_quote: No hand labels on the provided game, in any amount and for any purpose — not for the submission, not to train a model and not to validate one. The provided game is the test set.
implication: Target labels remain prohibited; external labels require rights and disclosure.

exact_quote: The 5 minutes published in this repository are for checking that your pipeline is correct — frames aligned, file well-formed, labels meaning what you think. They are not training data and not a tuning set.
implication: Public target truth is pipeline-check only.

exact_quote: Running your repository against the provided data must reproduce your submission. Not approximately — the same file.
implication: The full method must be reproducible.

exact_quote: Do not redistribute the data. That includes committing it to a public repository. Do not publish derived data that would reconstruct it.
implication: Competition data and reconstructible extracts remain outside Git.

exact_quote: External data must be about other games. Any human-produced data about the provided game — event data, corrected tracking, annotations, from any source — is not allowed. However, as the Terms and Conditions state, participants shall not upload, disclose or otherwise make available to any third-party hosted or cloud-based LLM any videos, datasets, confidential information or other restricted materials provided in connection with the Competition.
implication: External use remains subject to provider rights and target extracts remain prohibited from cloud services.

exact_quote: The organisers can access and inspect it. Anything in your pipeline has to be something we can look at and run — your repository, a public model, a commercial API, an open dataset. Your technical document explains it.
implication: Every model dataset and processing component must be inspectable and documented.
